data.name: Onofrio
data.gender_notes: Onofrio is used as a male name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Latin word 'onus' meaning 'burden' and 'fricare' meaning 'to rub', Onofrio is a name of endurance and patience. In Christian tradition, Onofrio is believed to be the name of a saint who was a disciple of St. Peter. The name Onofrio carries the meaning “Patience, Endurance” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Onofrio usually hope their child will grow to embody patience, endurance and live with faith, good character and purpose.

It is believed to be a name of nobility and strength, passed down through generations. The name is associated with a rich history and deep-rooted traditions. In Sicily, many towns and villages bear the name Onofrio, reflecting the cultural significance of this name.
data.spiritual_significance: In the Christian tradition, Onofrio is believed to be the name of a saint who was a disciple of St. Peter. According to legend, Onofrio was a Roman magistrate who was cured from his blindness by St. Peter. Moved by this miracle, Onofrio converted to Christianity and became a devoted disciple of St. Peter. He is revered as a patron saint of the blind and those suffering from eye diseases. Onofrio's spiritual significance lies in his unwavering faith and devotion to God, inspiring those who bear his name to embody his virtues of endurance and patience in their own lives.
